name: Rías Baixas
terms: Denominación de Origen, Spain's main quality tier.
Young wine, sold with little or no aging. Some see a few months in oak.
keyfacts: Rías Baixas is a DO in Galicia, granted in 1988, which replaced the Denominación Específica Albariño status given in 1980.
Albariño makes up more than 96% of the grapes harvested, and red grapes are less than 1%.
The DO has five sub-zones: Val do Salnés, O Rosal, Condado do Tea, Soutomaior and Ribeira do Ulla.
The climate is Atlantic, with mild temperatures, small temperature swings and about ⟦rain|51 inches|1,300 mm⟧ of rain a year, less in summer.
Vines are traditionally trained on high wire trellises called parras, held up by granite posts, to protect them from humidity and make better use of the sun.
Condado do Tea lies inland along the Miño and is warmer and drier than O Rosal, with summer highs that can reach ⟦temp|104°F|40°C⟧.

notes: Rías Baixas Albariño has complex aromas of citrus, flowers and fruit, with apple standing out.
On the palate it is balanced and fresh, with good structure, some richness and a floral, fruity finish.
Poor, sandy soils and a ripening season of modest sunshine and moderate temperatures give wines known more for their acidity and aroma than their alcohol.
Barrel-aged whites add toast, smoke, vanilla and nutty notes.
The reds are light in body and moderately tannic, with red berry and herbal aromas.

blurb.text: A Galician DO in Pontevedra and southern A Coruña provinces, known for white wines from the Albariño grape. Its subzones include Val do Salnés, O Rosal and Condado do Tea. Godello, Loureira and Treixadura are also allowed.
